concepts.label: XDCR Advanced Settings
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted this batch in xdcr-reference-intro.json; this is that concept's own defining/detailed page.

concepts.label: XDCR checkpoint document
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the per-vBucket artifact XDCR computes and persists during the Checkpoint Interval, recording the high sequence number successfully replicated; used to resume a restarted or recovered replication without redoing work. First contact.

concepts.label: XDCR Compression Type setting
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the Auto/None toggle controlling whether documents are compressed for XDCR transmission. First contact.

concepts.label: XDCR Optimistic Replication Threshold
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the compressed-document-size threshold below which XDCR skips source-side conflict resolution (fetching target metadata) and simply replicates, deferring conflict resolution to the target. First contact.

concepts.label: XDCR conflict resolution method (Sequence Number | Timestamp)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted in cloud/clusters/xdcr/xdcr.json. This page calls the values 'sequence number' and 'timestamp'; xdcr-filtering-reference-intro.md (same batch) calls the same choice 'revision-based' and 'timestamp-based' - see cross_component_finding.

concepts.label: Cross Cluster Versioning (CCV) bucket property
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - minted in cloud/clusters/xdcr/manage-xdcr-replications.json as a per-bucket property gating conflict logging and Active-Active/App Services replication. This page shows a third gated behavior: optimistic replication is available only while CCV is disabled.

relations.subject: xdcr:advanced-settings
relations.evidence: During this interval (which does not affect the persistence of data), XDCR computes and persists checkpoint documents, which contain the high sequence number for each vBucket successfully replicated to the target cluster.

relations.subject: xdcr:compression-type-setting
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (usesEnum) - subject and object coincide because the setting concept is also its own value set, same pattern as n1ql:scan-consistency in server/8.0/indexes/index-lifecycle.json
relations.evidence: The XDCR Compression Type setting can be either `Auto` or `None`.

relations.subject: xdcr:compression-type-setting
relations.evidence: When `Auto` is specified, data compression is attempted during replication only if the target cluster is running Couchbase Server 5.5 or a later version.

relations.subject: xdcr:optimistic-replication-threshold
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (requiresSetting) - the required value is CCV disabled, not merely 'configured'; noted in the evidence itself
relations.evidence: XDCR optimistic replication is applicable only when the enableCrossClusterVersioning property is disabled.

relations.subject: xdcr:optimistic-replication-threshold
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (dependsOnService) - loose structural dependency: the threshold decides whether conflict resolution happens on the source before replication
relations.evidence: For documents larger than so specified, XDCR fetches metadata from the target cluster, in order to perform conflict resolution on the source, prior to replication.

relations.subject: xdcr:conflict-resolution-method
relations.evidence: The default conflict resolution setting is based on _sequence number_.

notable_absence.finding: The entire Advanced Settings table - a dozen numeric/enum tuning knobs (nozzles, checkpoint interval, batch count/size, failure-retry interval, optimistic-replication threshold, network usage limit, logging level) - carries no Enterprise/Community edition badge and names no role or privilege anywhere. The only gate found on this page at all is the Server-5.5 threshold on the Compression Type 'Auto' behavior, and the CCV-disabled precondition on the optimistic-replication threshold. This is a purely mechanical tuning-parameter page: access-control content, if any exists for who may set these values, is deferred entirely to xdcr-filtering-reference-intro.md's 'Full, Cluster, and XDCR Administrators' line (not restated here) or to pages outside this batch.

cross_component_finding: NAMING INCONSISTENCY FOR THE SAME ENUM, WITHIN SERVER'S OWN DOCS (see also xdcr-filtering-reference-intro.json, same batch, for the mirror-image writeup). This page: 'The default conflict resolution setting is based on _sequence number_. Alternatively, conflict resolution based on _timestamp_ can be selected.' xdcr-filtering-reference-intro.md: 'Filtering ... can be used with either the _revision-based_ or the _timestamp-based_ conflict resolution policy.' Both describe the same fixed-at-bucket-creation choice modeled by the extraction-layer concept xdcr:conflict-resolution-method (values 'Sequence Number' / 'Timestamp', per cloud/clusters/xdcr/xdcr.json). 'Sequence number' and 'revision-based' are the same value under two names, one bullet apart in module terms - a same-mechanism-different-name split found between two sibling pages in this SAME batch, not across products.
